headers.//: The service worker script itself must never be long-cached: the browser's update check is what discovers a new build, and a cached copy would delay every deploy by the cache lifetime. no-cache still allows a 304, so the check costs one conditional request.

Rollup content-hashes everything under /assets, so a given filename can only ever hold one set of bytes — safe to cache forever, and it matches how sw.js serves them (cache-first, dropped wholesale when BUILD_ID changes). Hosting's default here is only max-age=3600, which made a return visit an hour later re-download the whole ~1 MB bundle.

Prerendered shells (dist/artist/*.html, dist/fandoms.html, dist/hall-of-fame.html) embed hourly rank data and reference hashed assets — always revalidate so a deploy or rank refresh is picked up immediately. Header globs match the REQUEST path, so the cleanUrls forms are listed alongside **/*.html.

redirects.//: Strips a trailing slash from the six fixed routes, which otherwise fell through the ** SPA rewrite to the plain index.html shell (its title/canonical, not the real route's) since no prerendered file matches a directory-style path. Deliberately NOT attempted for /artist/:id/ and /u/:handle/: Firebase Hosting's named :param capture treats a trailing slash in the source as optional, so that pattern matched the bare path too and 301'd it to itself — an infinite loop, caught only by testing against the hosting emulator before deploy, never in production. A ** wildcard source avoided the loop but its capture couldn't be referenced in the destination (:0 silently failed to match rather than substitute). Rather than guess further at unverified syntax in a config that fails by taking down every artist page, those two routes rely on the client-side canonical self-correction verified in Chrome: both title and <link rel=canonical> resolve correctly once React hydrates.
